sections.heading: Default structure
sections.text: Push-pull uses two switches driving a center-tapped transformer. Duty cycle must stay below 0.5 to prevent simultaneous conduction. Peak-current-mode control is strongly preferred over voltage-mode to handle flux imbalance and provide automatic current sharing.

sections.heading: Design formulas
sections.text: V_out = D*V_in*N_sec/N_pri (per half-cycle, D<0.5). Transformer turns ratio N = N_sec/N_pri sets the conversion ratio. Effective switching frequency at the output is 2*fsw. Reset volt-second = D*V_in/fsw per half-cycle.

sections.heading: Constraint
sections.text: Flux imbalance: even small duty-cycle asymmetry causes DC bias in the transformer core. Current-mode control with per-switch current sensing provides inherent flux balancing. Voltage-mode requires external flux-balance circuits. Add leading-edge blanking (100-300ns) to blank the MOSFET turn-on spike.

sections.heading: Escalation trigger
sections.text: If the push-pull shows flux imbalance (rising magnetizing current, core saturation), verify current sensing is per-switch (not averaged). If leakage inductance causes excessive voltage spikes, add snubbers or consider an active clamp. For higher power (>500W), consider half-bridge or full-bridge.
